page: Microsoft Azure FX4mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual server powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores running at 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations. The server is equipped with 84.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 21.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a 236 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results indicate highly asymmetric performance characteristics. The server achieves top-tier single-core performance, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2262.0 and strong single-threaded compression and decompression rates. However, multi-core performance is limited, with stress-ng multi-core and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression benchmarks falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth also exhibits a sharp contrast; while cached small-block reads perform at an average rate of 345.52 GB/sec, uncached large-block read and write speeds are weak, measuring 35.98 GB/sec and 25.58 GB/sec respectively.

From a resource-density perspective, the FX4mds_v2 offers a specialized qualitative cost profile, providing a massive memory footprint without requiring the purchase of excess vCPUs. This makes it highly efficient for memory-bound, low-concurrency workloads. It is well-suited for database operations, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and single-threaded text or data processing tasks. It is less suitable for heavily parallelized compute tasks, software compilation, or large-scale LLM text generation.
